what_this_is: Identities this market carries but will not publish, each one held by a named founder ruling and each one carrying the evidence a later order needs to resolve it. A hold is a MOVE of the question, never a deletion of the answer: every first-party capture behind these rows is preserved and cited.

what_a_later_order_needs_to_do: Confirm on a first-party source that 10667 and 10667B are two distinct lodging premises, not one building with two mailing forms.
If they are two: split the census row into two identities, carry the Days Inn refusal onto the 10667B identity, and re-read the Super 8 for a publication-grade statement -- 'Dog-friendly' is a chip.
If they are one: rule which brand trades there today and treat the other as a predecessor, retiring it by MOVE.
Either way the fix belongs upstream too: address_key drops the building letter, and any market with an A/B campus will hit this again.

preservation_guarantee: Nothing here is deleted. Every held identity remains in the census with its aliases, every read remains in the evidence audit with its quote and document provenance, and every route remains in the routing table. A later order inherits work already done and paid for.
